name: Amaranth Groats
imageAlt: dry raw amaranth seeds in a rustic small wooden scoop on a dark textured background
description: Amaranth groats are an ancient, completely gluten-free pseudocereal substrate derived from the dense, nutrient-packed seeds of Amaranthus cruentus or Amaranthus hypochondriacus. Highly distinct from traditional cereal grains, amaranth features a radically superior amino acid matrix centered around optimal concentrations of lysine. Enriched with squalene—a critical lipid-soluble antioxidant—and dense soluble fibers, it delivers phenomenal vascular endothelial protection and complete, non-reactive peptide absorption.
macroIntro: Amaranth exhibits a heavily balanced, protein-dense macronutrient matrix, combining premium essential peptides with high-quality unsaturated fatty acids and complex, slow-releasing starches.
microIntro: The amaranth seed houses an incredibly rich biochemical micro-matrix, boasting extraordinary volumes of squalene, organic iron, structural magnesium, and tissue-building calcium.

precautionsIntro: Oxalate Crystal Aggregations, Raw Saponin Antinutrient Buffers, and Gastrointestinal Adaptation Thresholds: Strategic thermal boiling secures metabolic safety.
precautions: Oxalate Mediated Renal Load: Amaranth contains measurable amounts of organic oxalates. Individuals with established calcium-oxalate kidney stone backgrounds must regulate portion scales and integrate optimal hydration protocols.

Raw Saponin and Phytate Complexes: The exterior coating of the seeds carries mild saponin bitters and phytic structures that can decrease trace element absorption. Thorough pre-rinsing and extended boiling completely deactivates these elements.

Intestinal Adaptation to Dense Fiber: Due to its dense, highly concentrated fiber and lipid matrix, unmanaged consumption can precipitate temporary bloating, soft stools, or mild cramping in sensitive gastrointestinal tracts.
